title: Spleen

compareCandidate.label: Spleen vs. kidney
compareCandidate.description: Both filter blood, but the kidney makes urine from wastes and controls water/salt balance, while the spleen recycles blood cells and fights germs - it makes no urine.

plainLanguageExplanation: The spleen is a small organ about the size of a fist, tucked under the ribs on the left side. It acts like a blood filter and immune checkpoint. It filters the blood, recycling old or damaged red blood cells and salvaging useful parts like iron. It also stores blood cells and platelets for when the body needs them. And it helps the immune system: white blood cells in the spleen can spot and respond to germs in the blood. If the spleen is removed, other organs can take over most of its jobs, though the person needs extra protection from some infections.

whyItMatters: The spleen keeps your blood clean and healthy and helps your immune system respond to germs. Understanding it shows how the body recycles its own materials and defends itself.
tagline: The body's blood filter and immune checkpoint
didYouKnow: The spleen recycles about one million old red blood cells every second, salvaging the iron to build new ones.
